title: Retention Remittance — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction
content:
# Retention remittance — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction

The retention remittance is the amount the borrower of record sends in person to the payoff case of a Borrower Voluntary Payoff requested by the borrower of record on a loan whose maturity case is due and payable, in its extension period or referred to foreclosure.

**Recording.** Each remittance is recorded once, identified by its remittance reference; a remittance the borrower of record sends in person on a retention payoff or as a short-sale seller contribution receives its remittance reference from the servicer when it is recorded, and is recorded once under that issued reference.

**Application, retained charges and refund.** On satisfaction exactly the required payoff amount is applied to the loan, as the plan's funds-application timing provides, and on a retention payoff, the payoff case of a Borrower Voluntary Payoff requested by the borrower of record on a loan whose maturity case is due and payable, in its extension period or referred to foreclosure, or on the payoff case of an Approved Short Sale Payoff requested by the borrower of record, the remittance charges collected with the borrower's own remittance, other than its clearing cushion, are then retained for those charges, and the clearing cushion, per diem collected in advance, is kept only for the per diem the case owes for each day its funds were credited after the statement's good-through date, as the plan's interest-through basis provides; any held excess left, an unused cushion included, is refunded within the plan's refund period of business days to the remitter of the receipt that took the pooled total over the required amount, up to that receipt's amount, and then to earlier remitters in reverse order of receipt, as the plan's refund-target setting provides.

**When the amount is worked out.** The retention remittance is worked out only once the payoff case carries an approved appraisal basis with its required payoff amount. A case that does not yet show an approved appraisal basis with its required payoff amount has no retention remittance figure.

## Sending the funds

**Capability.** The tool sends payoff funds in the customer's own name to their payoff case, recorded as one receipt that the case holds until the loan is paid off. The receipt is dated today, carries the method, sender name and amount given, and receives a newly issued remittance reference; the amount is added to the funds the case holds. On success the customer can see the receipt on the case and quote its remittance reference.

**How it is invoked.** `remit_borrower_payoff_funds_17f1493b` is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters.**

1. `payoff_case_id` — the reference number of the payoff case the funds are sent to, as given by the servicer.
2. `remittance_method` — how the funds are sent, one of: `wire` (a bank wire transfer to the servicer's payoff account); `cashiers_check` (a cashier's check delivered to the servicer); `check` (a check the servicer itself issues when it pays money out, never used for funds a customer sends); `not_applicable` (an entry where no cash moves, never used for funds a customer sends).
3. `remitter_name` — the sender's full name exactly as the customer states it for the funds, copied character for character.
4. `amount` — the amount sent, in USD with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent.

**Return.** A confirmation naming the payoff case reference number, the receipt reference number, the issued remittance reference, the method, the sender name and the amount (USD, 2 decimal places), and the funds now held on the case (USD, 2 decimal places); the word "received" shows the funds were recorded. No other return or error is defined for this tool.
